Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Family history of lung cancer may increase sensitivity to respiratory symptoms and catastrophic interpretations.
- Precipitating factors: Acute onset of sore throat and dry cough with intermittent exertional shortness of breath; initial fever; online searching leading to heightened concern about serious disease.
- Perpetuating factors: Fluctuating symptom course; uncertainty; limited objective examination in teleconsult; ongoing work disruption.
- Protective factors: Proactive help-seeking; acceptance of reassurance and safety-net advice; employment structure.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce worry about serious illness; obtain clear guidance and reassurance; manage distress while recovering; return to work when symptoms allow.
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide psychoeducation about typical illness course and health-related anxiety; introduce brief coping strategies; monitor for persistence/escalation of anxiety beyond illness resolution; coordinate follow-up if needed.
- Actions (Patient): 
  - Limit unhelpful online health searches; use reputable sources if needed.
  - Practice simple breathing/relaxation techniques during spikes of worry.
  - Monitor symptoms and follow safety-net advice for medical red flags.
  - Seek follow-up if health-related worry persists after physical symptoms improve.
- Actions (Clinician/GP): 
  - Reinforce reassurance and safety-netting; provide clear return/ER criteria.
  - Consider brief screening (e.g., GAD-7) if anxiety persists or impairs functioning.
  - Offer/consider referral for brief CBT focused on health anxiety if symptoms persist.
  - Continue medical management of acute respiratory illness (paracetamol, rest, fluids; sick note provided).

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Patient Goal(s): Manage occupational impact and return to work safely.
- Clinical Goal(s): Support graded return to work as physical symptoms improve; reduce anxiety related to work absence.
- Actions (Patient): Use provided sick note; communicate with employer regarding return timeline.
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide/extend fit note as clinically indicated; reassess functional capacity if symptoms persist.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Reassurance regarding likely benign course of acute respiratory illness; safety-net advice; self-care measures (rest, fluids, paracetamol). Specific mental health education not recorded.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating preoccupation with serious illness; increasing online searches; new or worsening insomnia; persistent anxiety after physical recovery; new functional impairment.
- Coping Strategies: Limit online searches; scheduled worry time; paced breathing; routine daily structure; contact GP if anxiety persists or worsens.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded.
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded.
- Review Date: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- The provided DDx addressed physical respiratory conditions only (e.g., acute viral URI/bronchitis, reactive airway disease) and did not include mental health differential diagnoses. No mental health DDx available from the provided source.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal mental health diagnosis, full MSE, suicide/self-harm risk assessment, validated screening measures (e.g., PHQ-9/GAD-7), explicit consent, review date, and emergency contact are not recorded.  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: DOB given as 09/05/2016 conflicts with adult social history and employment (conflict noted). Inconsistent reporting around chest pain and shortness of breath (initial “no” then “yes”).  
● Transcript quality notes: Teleconsultation with time constraints; some ambiguous/overlapping dialogue; no vitals or in-person exam; session ended abruptly due to time.
